'''Yael Karshon''' ({{Langx|he|יעל קרשון}}; born 1964){{r|born}} is an Israeli and Canadian mathematician who has been described as "one of Canada's leading experts in [[symplectic geometry]]".{{r|3h}}
She works as a professor at the [[University of Toronto Mississauga]] {{r|profile}} and [[Tel Aviv University]] {{r|israelProfile}}.

==Education and career==
Karshon took part in the 1982 [[International Mathematical Olympiad]], on the Israeli team.{{r|imo}}
She earned her Ph.D. in 1993 from [[Harvard University]] under the supervision of [[Shlomo Sternberg]].{{r|3h|mgp}}

After working as a [[C. L. E. Moore instructor]] at the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]], and then earning tenure at the [[Hebrew University of Jerusalem]], she moved to the University of Toronto Mississauga in 2002.{{r|3h}}

==Selected publications==
Karshon is the author of the monographs ''Periodic Hamiltonian flows on four dimensional manifolds'' (Memoirs of the American Mathematical Society 672, 1999), which completely classified the [[Hamiltonian action]]s of the [[circle group]] on four-dimensional [[compact manifold]]s.{{r|woodward}} With [[Viktor Ginzburg]] and [[Victor Guillemin]], she also wrote ''Moment maps, cobordisms, and Hamiltonian group actions'' (Mathematical Surveys and Monographs 98, American Mathematical Society, 2002), which surveys "symplectic geometry in the context of equivariant cobordism".{{r|holm}}

==Awards and honours==
Karshon won the [[Krieger–Nelson Prize]] in 2008.{{r|3h}}

==Personal==
Karshon is from Israel, and lived in the US for ten years, eventually becoming a permanent resident. She took Canadian citizenship in 2011.
From her marriage to mathematician [[Dror Bar-Natan]]{{r|dbn}} she has two sons.
